definition: Formal dinner held in the Commons once a semester to honor our Associates.
The process used to assign rooms for the next year.
The week preceding Beer Bike, filled with college activities, alumni, and jacks.
The spreading of Halloween cheer, led by the elected College Idiots. Features Halloween songs and visits to the other colleges.
Where you get your food before you go sit down in the Commons. We share South Servery with Hanszen.
The weekend retreat to Galveston during the fall semester to bond with other Wiessmen.
An affectionate name for the Wiess powderpuff football team.
Our one and only cheer. It is one of our oldest traditions, and an embodiment of the spirit Wiess has always been known for.
The governing body of Wiess, made up entirely of Wiessmen. It meets every other Wednesday at 9 pm in the Upper Commons. There’s always free food.
Party to celebrate the new Cabinet each year during the spring semester.
The place to be. You will eat here, study here, act here, play here, party here, hang out here, and well, live here.
To pull up an extra chair at the corner of a table. Frequently occurs during meals.
A corner of the commons featuring extremely comfortable couches, a large goldenrod rug, a small table, and several napping OC students.

The people who make O-Week possible. They are some of the greatest people you will ever meet and care about you so much. Co-Fellows are Fellows from other colleges. These other colleges may confuse you by calling them “Advisors,” but we don’t call them that.
Required service hours. Necessary to enter the housing jack at the end of your first year. There are plenty of opportunities throughout the year to get them!
The official Wiess color. It will soon dominate your wardrobe. Remember, it’s not yellow!
The ones who have been planning O-Week since January: [three names omitted]. Say hello if you see them around!
An abbreviation of Team Family (or anything else that starts with F) Wiess.
Team Fun Friday Wiess. Held every other week, this event features food and fun for everyone in the Acabowl. What other colleges call Friday in the Quad (FITQ).
A unique Wiess celebration of life. If you have any questions, just ask a friendly Wiessman.
Wiess mascot; embodied by the giant wooden pig built by the Class of 2012 for Beer Bike.
Flavio and Fabiana’s home. Where everybody knows your name, and the door is always open.
The inclusive, gender-neutral term for all members of Wiess—including you.
Alternative Spring Break; a service trip over spring break based on a social issue.
Rice Student Volunteer Program. The organization that runs many community service opportunities beyond the hedges.
Critical Dialogues on Diversity. A required course for new students to embrace diversity at Rice.
Critical Thinking in Sexuality. A required course for new students to provide information about consent, relationships, and bystander training.
First-Year Writing-Intensive Seminar. Writing course students are required to take in their first year.
Graduate Student Association.
Housing and Dining. The Administrative office in charge of all food service and residential buildings on campus.
Rice’s student-run radio station, which now streams online. Plays everything from jazz to reggae to bands you probably didn’t even know existed.
Lifetime Physical Activity Program. A required “gym” class that all students must take to graduate.
Off-campus. Typically your second year at Wiess.
Rice University Police Department. Save their number for emergencies: 713-348-6000.
Student Association. The campus-wide body representing students. Deals with campus-wide issues and administrative business.
Marching Owl Band. They don’t actually march. They do, however, always put on an entertaining show during halftime—filled with amusing skits, jibes at opposing teams, and zany antics.

A competitive intercollege race held in the spring, where ten bikers and ten chuggers from each college compete for both personal and college pride. Often compared to Christmas, it also includes a water balloon fight and much rejoicing.
BioScience Research Collaborative, where Rice meets the Texas Medical Center for research. Also where Bioengineers spend most of their time for class starting junior year.
A modernistic glass building located behind Fondren. Home to a non-student operated bakery and café and a great place to relax and sit outside.
Student-run coffeeshop providing the best legal way to artificially increase your study skills on short notice. Located in the RMC.
Also known as Club Fondy, Fondren is Rice’s library—it has seminar rooms, study rooms, and classrooms that you can reserve.
The one-way road that loops around the center of campus.
Rice University Emergency Medical Services. Rice students that are trained as Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) who respond to emergencies on campus.
Rice Memorial Center; where you can find the Bookstore, Coffeehouse, Pub, and important offices like Academic Advising.
Rice Program Council. The organization in charge of university-wide events such as Beer Bike, Screw-Yer-Roommate, Esperanza, and study breaks during finals.
Rice’s Graduate School of Business, not to be confused with Jones College.
The university computer center. If you have problems with your computer, the IT (Information Technology) people here are glad to help out. Also a great place to print large posters.
The 5 kilometer loop that surrounds all of Rice University. Students often run along the path surrounding the loop.
Willy’s Pub, located in the basement of the RMC. A great place to grab some pizza and hang out with people across campus. Heavily populated on Thursday nights.
The “real world” outside of Rice.
A faculty, staff, or community member associated with a college. Good people to get to know.
The big archway in Lovett Hall. Rumor says that if you walk through it between matriculation and graduation, you won’t graduate.
1. The bell tower in the Engineering Quad. 2. Rice’s yearbook. 3. The undergraduate orchestra for non-music majors.
The pyramidal installation located next to the Shepherd School of Music. A great place to watch the sunrise and sunset.

Refers to distribution credits, Rice’s way of making sure you get a balanced education. You need at least 9 credit hours in each category to graduate. D1 = Humanities, D2 = Social Sciences, and D3 = Science and Engineering.
A student-run late night food stop for hungry students which is located in the RMC.
The area in the Medical Center with many restaurants that Rice students frequent.
Barbara and David Gibbs Recreation and Wellness Center. Fully equipped for all of your workout needs. Also where the Wellbeing and Counseling Center is located.
The shopping center west of campus. Has a lot of great restaurants and shops, all within walking distance!

An event where participants undress, smear shaving cream on their bodies, and run around campus, leaving a trail of body prints. A proud Baker tradition for over thirty years; all undergrads are invited to participate.
A prank pulled on another college.
Women’s college flag football. One of the most intense (and fun) college sports, as well as a great spectator sport. Played in the fall semester.
Mid-semester grades given to new students in the fall to indicate how they are doing in their classes. They come out around Halloween.
A harsh penalty banning a student from campus except for attending classes and exams. Basically, don’t get rusticated.
The Rice mascot.
The fall formal hosted by Rice Program Council. A major part of homecoming weekend and lots of fun!

Informal, low-stress sports played among students. Not to be confused with college sports, which are played between teams representing each of the colleges with points going towards the President’s Cup.
The ceremony held during O-Week to officially welcome you to Rice.
Spring formal hosted by Rice Program Council.
Also known as Screw. A Rice tradition held in the fall in which roommates set up blind dates for each other.
Points, or “Digital Money” on your ID card that can be used at various on-campus restaurants/cafés.
Rice’s weekly student newspaper.
Your home and family.
